Search terms for this lesson“why can I jump forever in mid-air?”Guided build

In 6.1 your jump impulse worked — so well that mashing J flew straight to the ceiling. Today we cap jumps with jumpsRemaining and refill it only when OnCollisionEnter2D() hits an object tagged "Ground".

Break It Down~10 minGuided build

Stop the player from jumping infinitely in mid-air — give them one jump per landing.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Track how many jumps are leftAdd int jumpsRemaining; and int maxJumps = 1; to PlayerController, initialized to maxJumps inside Start() when entering a platformer scene.Read: 2.1 (int fields in the class body) and Start() in 6.1
  2. write this partRead: the Update() jump gate in the walkthrough below (KeyCode.J + jumpsRemaining >= 1)
  3. Refill jumps when touching tagged GroundIn OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D other), check other.gameObject.CompareTag("Ground") and reset jumpsRemaining = maxJumps;.Read: Unity OnCollisionEnter2D() & CompareTag() in 2.1 / quick reference

Notice the pattern from 2.1 and 3.3 coming back: you already stopped infinite firing with cooldownTimer. Here you stop infinite jumping with an integer counter (jumpsRemaining), spend 1 inside Update(), and refill it inside a solid collision callback (OnCollisionEnter2D()) whenever the player touches an object tagged "Ground".

Your turn

Before writing code, explain what breaks if you reset jumpsRemaining = maxJumps inside OnCollisionEnter2D() WITHOUT checking CompareTag("Ground") first.

Why do we check other.gameObject.CompareTag("Ground") instead of other.CompareTag("Ground") inside OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D other)?

In the Editor ~10 min

Before writing C#, make sure Unity has a Ground tag and your platformer floor carries it:

  1. Open Assets/Scenes/Platformer.unity. Select any GameObject in the Inspector → click the Tag dropdown → Add Tag... → create a tag named Ground (exact spelling and capital G).
  2. Assign the Ground tag to your floor platforms (or Tilemap collider object in the cave).
  3. Confirm the floor collider has Is Trigger UNCHECKED, because OnCollisionEnter2D() only fires for solid collisions — triggers fire OnTriggerEnter2D() instead.
  4. Test pressing J twice in the air after updating the script: the first press fires, the second ignores you until feet touch "Ground".
Two common bugs when jumps stop refilling:
  • Wrong Tag spelling or left on Untagged: CompareTag("Ground") fails silently or throws an error if the tag does not exist in Tag Manager.
  • Wall touching resets jumps: if a vertical wall shares the "Ground" tag and uses the same collider, brushing against the side wall can count as landing. Put separate walls on an untagged or "Wall" object, or test how your level behaves.

Socratic: Collision Counters vs. Continuous Checks

  1. Why does setting rb.linearVelocityX = xVector; instead of rb.linearVelocity = new Vector2(xVector, 0); matter when the player jumps or falls?
  2. Why is jumpsRemaining better as an int counter starting at maxJumps = 1 instead of a bool canJump?
  3. What happens if the player walks off a ledge WITHOUT jumping first — what is jumpsRemaining still set to in mid-air, and is that a bug or an intentional feel choice?
In the CodeGuided build

The question this answers“why can I jump forever in mid-air?”

You are editing Assets/Scripts/PlayerController.cs. Open Assets/Scripts/PlayerController.cs. You already added isPlatformer, gravityScale, and Jump() in 6.1. Fill in the jump counter, spend it in Update(), and refill it on "Ground" collisions.

Step 1Declare the jump budget fields and initialize in Start()

Add two integer fields in PlayerController and initialize jumpsRemaining = maxJumps; inside the platformer branch of Start().

    int jumpsRemaining;
    int maxJumps = 1;

  3. 4Inside the else (platformer) branch of Start() from 6.1.

Step 2Gate the jump key and spend one jump

Replace the old jump if inside the platformer branch (else of if (!isPlatformer)) so pressing J only fires when jumpsRemaining >= 1, then decrements jumpsRemaining.

        if (!isPlatformer)

            rb.linearVelocity = new Vector2(xVector, yVector);
        }
        else
        {
            if (____ && ____)

  1. 1Top-down branch from Overworld: full 2D new Vector2(xVector, yVector) movement.
  2. 3Keeps top-down movement untouched.
  3. 5Platformer branch: jump on KeyCode.J, and only overwrite horizontal rb.linearVelocityX so gravity owns vertical falling.

Your turn7Write the jump gate: require BOTH the KeyCode.J press this frame AND at least 1 jump left in your counter.Reach for Input.GetKeyDown(), KeyCode.J, and your jumpsRemaining field.Two facts have to agree before physics pushes upward. Using isPlatformer put us inside this else branch; checking the jump budget stops mid-air climbing without blocking future multi-jump upgrades.
  5. 9Runs your existing Jump() impulse method.
  6. 10Spends 1 jump immediately so pressing J a second time in mid-air fails the >= 1 check.

Step 3Refill jumpsRemaining on Ground collision

Add OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D other) below OnTriggerExit2D() so landing on any solid collider tagged "Ground" restores jumpsRemaining.

    void OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D other)
    {
        if (other.gameObject.CompareTag("Ground"))
        {
            jumpsRemaining = maxJumps;
        }
    }
  1. 1Called automatically by Unity Physics 2D when two solid (non-trigger) colliders start touching.
  2. 3Checks the Tag on the GameObject you landed on.Not every solid object is a floor. Walls, enemies, and moving barriers can also trigger OnCollisionEnter2D(); checking CompareTag("Ground") prevents wall-jumping off anything unintended.
  3. 5Restores the jump count so the player can jump again once grounded.
Check your work: the finished filetry every gap first — then open this to compare

Look how small that architecture is: NO raycast, NO LayerMask, and the else branch setting rb.linearVelocityX = xVector; preserves gravity's downward acceleration every frame while keeping if (!isPlatformer) ready for top-down movement and ladders.

// ------------------------------------------------------------------
//  REFERENCE FILE — Assets/Scripts/PlayerController.cs
//  Written to be read, not pasted. Build it with the walkthrough
//  above, one step at a time, then open this and compare.
//  If it is sitting in your project unchanged, that is the thing
//  to go and do now — the walkthrough is still above you.
// ------------------------------------------------------------------
// Relevant fields and methods in PlayerController.cs (6.2)
    int jumpsRemaining;
    int maxJumps = 1;

    [SerializeField] float jumpForce;
    bool isPlatformer = false;
    [SerializeField] float gravityScale;

    void Start()
    {
        // ... GetComponent lookups from 1.6 / 2.2 / 2.7 ...
        Scene currentScene = SceneManager.GetActiveScene();
        if (currentScene.name == "Overworld")
        {
            rb.gravityScale = 0;
            isPlatformer = false;
        }
        else
        {
            rb.gravityScale = gravityScale;
            isPlatformer = true;
            jumpsRemaining = maxJumps;
            print(jumpsRemaining);
        }
    }

    void Update()
    {
        // ... read xDirection / yDirection -> xVector / yVector ...
        if (!isPlatformer)
        {
            rb.linearVelocity = new Vector2(xVector, yVector);
        }
        else
        {
            if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.J) && jumpsRemaining >= 1)
            {
                Jump();
                jumpsRemaining -= 1;
            }
            rb.linearVelocityX = xVector;
        }
    }

    void OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D other)
    {
        if (other.gameObject.CompareTag("Ground"))
        {
            jumpsRemaining = maxJumps;
        }
    }
